difficulty.notes: sm-crypto (module 193c) wraps module 8060 (sm2/sm3). Password uses sm32 (n = sm2(sm3(x))); username uses sm2nokey (i) directly, so i is shared by both paths (not a clean username-only decoy). The call-site accountSubmit is NOT in the oracle because it contains password-strength regex literals ({8,64}, {5}, char classes) that the static brace-balance check cannot validate as a complete function; the dispatcher c serves as the call-path role instead.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The sm32 function (n) that composes sm3 then sm2 to produce the password token; not the dispatcher c, the sm2 helper i, or the submit handler.

behavior_category.subtype: password via SM3-then-SM2 (sm32); username via SM2 (sm2nokey)
behavior_category.recompute_check: SM2 encryption is randomized; not reproducible to a fixed value

near_categories.why_not: A single credential field (password) is tokenized; this is a per-field token derivation.
The value is keyed SM crypto of user input, not a UI-state encoding.

evidence: Minified webpack bundle (single-letter functions n/i/o/c); the sm-crypto wrapper is one module among many.
Password (sm32 -> n) and username (sm2nokey -> i) share the sm2 helper; n vs i vs c (dispatcher) are easy to confuse.
The dispatcher c selects the scheme by an EncryptType enum value; the actual algorithm is two modules deep (193c -> 8060).

provenance.label_points_to: the minified original (line 12); the on-disk file is beautified, so locate by content not by line:col
